This formula collection supports you during the Investment Finance lecture in the Bachelor of Business and Engineering program at THWS.

# Abbreviations

| Abbreviation | Explanation |
|--------------|-------------|
| $C$ | Equal periodic payment (annuity); coupon payment |
| $C_0$ | Initial loan capital (Chapter 3); Kapitalwert / NPV (Chapters 5–6) |
| $C_1$ | First payment of a growing perpetuity |
| $c$ | Coupon rate |
| $CF_t$ | Cash flow / Net inflow in period $t$ |
| $CRF$ | Capital Recovery Factor (Annuitätenfaktor) |
| $d$ | Annual value / Annuity of excess return |
| $D$ | Debt value |
| $D_1$ | Expected dividend in the next period |
| $D_t$ | Depreciation in period $t$ |
| $Div$ | Fixed (perpetual) dividend |
| $E$ | Equity value |
| $F$ | Par value / Face value of a bond |
| $FV$ | Future Value |
| $g$ | Growth rate |
| $i$ | Interest rate / Discount rate |
| $i_{after}$ | After-tax discount rate |
| $i_{nom}$ | Nominal annual interest rate |
| $i_{rel}$ | Relative (intra-year) interest rate |
| $I_0$ | Initial investment |
| $k$ | Number of sub-annual interest periods (beyond complete years) |
| $k_D$ | Cost of debt |
| $k_E$ | Cost of equity |
| $K_t$ | Debt service (total payment) in period $t$ |
| $L_n$ | Liquidation / Residual value at end of project |
| $m$ | Number of interest periods per year |
| $n$ | Duration / Term |
| $NPV$ | Net Present Value (Kapitalwert / $C_0$) |
| $P_0$ | Asset price / Bond price at $t = 0$ |
| $PI$ | Profitability Index |
| $PV$ | Present Value |
| $PVIFA$ | Present Value Interest Factor of an Annuity (Rentenbarwertfaktor) |
| $r$ | Rate of return / Yield to Maturity / IRR |
| $R_{t-1}$ | Remaining debt at the beginning of period $t$ |
| $s$ | Tax rate |
| $t$ | Point in time / Period |
| $T_t$ | Principal repayment in period $t$ |
| $Z_t$ | Interest payment in period $t$ |
| $\pi$ | Inflation rate |

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Interest Calculation

## Fisher Equation

Approximate relationship between nominal rate, inflation, and real rate:

$$ r \approx i_{nom} - \pi $$

For high rates (above ~10 %), use the exact form:

$$ 1 + r = \frac{1 + i_{nom}}{1 + \pi} $$

## Simple Interest (without compounding)

$$ FV = PV \cdot (1 + n \cdot i) $$

## Compound Interest

$$ FV = PV \cdot (1 + i)^n $$

## Discounting

The inverse of compounding — transports a future value back to the present:

$$ PV = FV \cdot (1+i)^{-n} = \frac{FV}{(1+i)^n} $$

The factor $(1+i)^{-n}$ is the **Discount Factor** (Abzinsungsfaktor); it is always less than 1 for $i > 0$.

## Nominal vs. Effective Interest (Intra-year Compounding)

Relative interest rate for intra-year periods ($m$ = periods per year):

$$ i_{rel} = \frac{i_{nom}}{m} $$

### Simple Interest (Intra-year)

$n$ = complete years, $k$ = additional sub-annual periods:

$$ FV = PV \cdot \bigl(1 + (n \cdot m + k) \cdot i_{rel}\bigr) $$

### Compound Interest (Intra-year)

$$ FV = PV \cdot (1 + i_{rel})^{n \cdot m + k} $$

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Annuities & Perpetuities

## Ordinary Annuity (Nachschüssige Rente)

Present value of $n$ equal **end-of-period** payments of $C$:

$$ PV = C \cdot PVIFA(i,\,n) $$

Annual payment required to amortise or generate a lump sum $PV$:

$$ C = PV \cdot CRF(i,\,n) $$

## Annuity Due (Vorschüssige Rente)

Payments occur at the **start** of each period (e.g. rent, leasing). Every payment is one period earlier, so the present value is higher by the factor $(1+i)$:

$$ PV_{\text{due}} = PV_{\text{ordinary}} \times (1+i) $$

## Present Value Interest Factor of an Annuity (PVIFA)

$$ PVIFA(i,\,n) = \frac{(1+i)^n - 1}{i \cdot (1+i)^n} $$

## Capital Recovery Factor (CRF)

$$ CRF(i,\,n) = \frac{i \cdot (1+i)^n}{(1+i)^n - 1} = \frac{1}{PVIFA(i,\,n)} $$

## Perpetuity

Present value of an infinite uniform payment stream:

$$ PV = \frac{C}{i} $$

## Growing Perpetuity

Present value of an infinite stream where payments grow at constant rate $g$ ($g < i$):

$$ PV = \frac{C_1}{i - g} $$

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Loan Amortization

## Debt Service

Every loan payment consists of an interest and a repayment component:

$$ K_t = Z_t + T_t \qquad \text{with } Z_t = R_{t-1} \cdot i $$

## Annuity Loan (Annuitätendarlehen)

Constant total payment per period (*Scissors Effect*: interest falls, repayment rises):

$$ K_t = C_0 \cdot CRF(i,\,n) = \text{constant} $$

## Constant Amortization Loan (Ratentilgungsdarlehen)

Equal principal repayment each period; total payment decreases linearly:

$$ T_t = \frac{C_0}{n} = \text{constant}, \qquad K_t = T_t + Z_t \quad \text{(declining)} $$

## Bullet Loan (Endfälliges Darlehen)

Interest-only payments throughout; full principal repaid at maturity:

$$ T_{1 \dots n-1} = 0, \qquad T_n = C_0, \qquad Z_t = C_0 \cdot i = \text{constant} $$

## Supplier Credit: Effective Interest Rate (Skonto)

$$ r_{\text{eff}} = \frac{s_k}{100 - s_k} \cdot \frac{360}{t_{\text{net}} - t_{\text{discount}}} \cdot 100 $$

where $s_k$ = cash discount percentage, $t_{\text{net}}$ = net payment term (days), $t_{\text{discount}}$ = early-payment term (days).

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Valuation

## Bond Valuation

A bond's price equals the present value of its coupon annuity plus the discounted par value ($C = F \cdot c$):

$$ P_0 = C \cdot PVIFA(r,\,n) + F \cdot (1+r)^{-n} $$

**Inverse problem — YTM from price (Linear Interpolation / Regula Falsi):**

$$ r \approx r_1 + \frac{P(r_1) - P_0}{P(r_1) - P(r_2)} \cdot (r_2 - r_1) $$

## Preferred Stock (Perpetuity)

Fixed dividend $Div$ in perpetuity:

$$ P_0 = \frac{Div}{r} $$

## Common Stock — Dividend Discount Model (Gordon Growth Model)

Dividends growing at constant rate $g$ in perpetuity ($g < r$):

$$ P_0 = \frac{D_1}{r - g} \qquad \text{with } D_1 = D_0 \cdot (1+g) $$

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Net Present Value

$$ NPV = -I_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{n} CF_t \cdot (1+i)^{-t} + L_n \cdot (1+i)^{-n} $$

| $NPV$ | Decision |
|:-----:|:--------:|
| $> 0$ | **Accept** — project creates value above cost of capital |
| $= 0$ | Indifferent — project exactly covers cost of capital |
| $< 0$ | **Reject** — project destroys value relative to market |

# Internal Rate of Return

The IRR $r$ is the discount rate at which $NPV = 0$:

$$ C_0 = -I_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{n} \frac{CF_t}{(1+r)^t} = 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{solve for } r $$

**Linear Interpolation (Regula Falsi):** choose $i_1$ with $C_0(i_1) > 0$ and $i_2$ with $C_0(i_2) < 0$:

$$ r \approx i_1 + \frac{C_0(i_1)}{C_0(i_1) - C_0(i_2)} \cdot (i_2 - i_1) $$

| $r$ vs. $i$ | Decision |
|:-----------:|:--------:|
| $r > i$ | **Accept** |
| $r = i$ | Indifferent |
| $r < i$ | **Reject** |

> Use NPV instead of IRR if the cash flow stream changes sign more than once (Descartes' Rule).

# Annuity Method

The **annual value** $d$ spreads the NPV evenly across the project's useful life:

$$ d = NPV \cdot CRF(i,\,n) $$

A positive $d$ means the project earns more than $i$ in every single year.

> Compare projects with **different lifespans** using $d$ rather than NPV — provided the shorter project can be repeated on equivalent terms.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Investment Appraisal with Taxes

## After-Tax Cash Flow — Volume Effect

$$ CF_{after} = CF_{before} \cdot (1 - s) + D_t \cdot s $$

The term $D_t \cdot s$ is the **Depreciation Tax Shield**.

## After-Tax Discount Rate — Interest Effect

$$ i_{after} = i_{before} \cdot (1 - s) $$

The Interest Tax Shield lowers the effective cost of debt, raising the present value of future cash flows.

## Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)

For mixed equity/debt financing:

$$ r_{WACC} = k_E \cdot \frac{E}{E+D} + k_D \cdot (1-s) \cdot \frac{D}{E+D} $$

# Capital Rationing — Dean Model

## Profitability Index (PI)

Value created per unit of invested capital:

$$ PI = \frac{NPV + I_0}{I_0} = 1 + \frac{NPV}{I_0} $$

| $PI$ | Decision |
|:----:|:--------:|
| $> 1$ | **Accept** — project creates value |
| $= 1$ | Indifferent ($NPV = 0$) |
| $< 1$ | **Reject** |

Under a **binding budget constraint**, rank all projects by $PI$ (descending) and fill the budget from the top. Ranking by absolute $NPV$ can crowd out efficient smaller projects (*Elephant Trap*).
